comment: Absolutely awesome. Taken for both Bio 229 and 313. He is incredibly passionate about his students and his coursework. Very understanding and puts in lots of effort to help his students succeed. Always available for extra help outside of class. Material can be challenging but he is always ready to help.

Dr. Harwich really makes you work for every point that you get. This class is tough if you don't come in with prior biology knowledge. It is not impossible to catch up to the class if you haven't, but you have to work for it. This class is extremely lecture-heavy and quick-moving. The lab is incredibly simple and he does a great job teaching lab.

Dr. Harwich has definitely been one of my favorite professors at UR so far. His lectures - although long - are super clear and the test material is based on the powerpoints so as long as you take notes and study you should do well. He did recommend purchasing the textbook but I didn't and don't feel the need to.

Harwich may have started off in a rough spot at UR, but he has absolutely improved his BIOL199. His lectures are information-heavy, but the tradeoff there is that his tests are mainly, if not completely, based off of the powerpoints and require little to no supplementation from videos/the textbook. I'd absolutely take his classes again.

I have nothing but great things to say about him. His lectures are heavy, but he is so enthusiastic and into them it makes you want to learn. His exams are not extremely difficult if you know what he has taught - he also will let you know what you should study the most! He also responds to emails swiftly and is super accessible outside of class!

Dr. Harwich gives a lot of work but he is a very knowledgeable man. Definitely knows what he's talking about and will make sure that you're accountable for a lot of content on the tests. He is very helpful outside of class and responses to emails promptly. Overall really cares about his students. Just make sure you study A LOT!

I think Harwich has gotten an undeserved bad rap on here. He's new at the school, and from what I've heard, his teaching style and its application to Richmond's culture specifically has gotten a lot better since early on. I'd call it the same difficulty as most 300 bio classes at UR.
He is really good! I took his class as a gen-ed. You just need to understand his teaching style and you'll realize he understands the audience and tweaks lectures to suit non-bio majors.

Lectures are only heavy bc they are compressive of the material & therefore only require little supplemental reading with the textbook. They are also much more interesting then sitting & reading. He expects students to be invested in material, but also works hard to make the info digestible & interesting. Love him as a professor!! 10/10 in my book

The level of prior knowledge that he expects you to have is absolutely ridiculous. I was really excited to take this class, but now I wish I would've dropped in the beginning like some others. The tests are really hard....I studied for weeks and still feel like I have absolutely no idea want he wants from us. Lab is a mess. Lots of work. sad.

Hands down the worst professor I have had at UR. The workload is unreasonable and his expectations are too high. The majority of the class dropped within the first few weeks of school and I wish I had done the same. Consistently runs over lecture time and doesn't do a great job of teaching. This class is a semester of work alone. Do not take.

I've only had him for a few weeks but he's already made his mark as one of the worst profs I've had at UR. His expectations for our prior knowledge and workload are so unreasonable that 1/3 of the class had already dropped within 2 weeks. His lab is bad, his lecture is bad, and the workload for his class is extremely unreasonable. Overall awful.
